                    ### Question
                    A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain has been isolated at a retirement home. Many of the elderly had been infected with this strain and are experiencing shingles. Which of the following would be the best antiviral agent to treat this population?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Acyclovir
opb. Famciclovir
opc. Ganciclovir
opd. Cidofovir
ope. Amantadine

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
For the elderly population infected with a thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain causing shingles, acyclovir may have reduced efficacy due to the virus strain's reduced susceptibility. Famciclovir may also be less effective due to potential cross-resistance with acyclovir. Ganciclovir is not recommended as the virus strain lacks thymidine kinase. Cidofovir could be considered as it does not require viral thymidine kinase for activation. Amantadine, targeting a different viral protein, might also be a potential option. Evidence paths support the use of acyclovir, famciclovir, ganciclovir, cidofovir, and amantadine in treating herpes zoster disease caused by the virus.
